themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying trees in CD 108 spiked to 4 complaints last week—a 3,100% increase versus the 8-week average of 0.1 complaints per week—suggesting either a recent disease outbreak, storm damage, or sudden lack of maintenance affecting the Upper East Side's urban canopy.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72, highest statistical severity)
Spike is isolated to this week only, indicating acute rather than chronic issue
311 data shows concentrated complaint pattern suggesting geographic cluster
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent storms, pests (emerald ash borer, Asian longhorned beetle), or disease caused sudden tree die-off along major blocks
Interview Parks Department about maintenance backlog and emergency response timeline; compare CD 108 tree health to other UES neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints jumped 600% to 7 last week versus 1.0 weekly average, and street sign missing complaints spiked 380% to 6 complaints 2 weeks ago—together suggesting coordinated or weather-related infrastructure failure affecting neighborhood navigation and safety.
evidence: Street sign damaged: 7 complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.9, 600% spike)
Street sign missing: 6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.91, 380% spike)
Combined pattern spans last 2 weeks, indicating ongoing rather than one-off event
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm or vehicle collision event that damaged signage systematically across a corridor?
Interview DOT about response times to missing/damaged sign complaints and whether CD 108 has a backlog

themes_detail.label: Litter and Public Space Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket complaints surged 700% to 3 complaints last week versus 0.4 weekly average, paired with a 500% spike in park rules violations (3 vs. 0.5) and 220% jump in animal complaints in parks (8 vs. 2.5)—indicating deteriorating park maintenance and public space conditions this week.
evidence: Litter basket complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, 700% spike)
Violation of park rules: 3 last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.54, 500% spike)
Animal in a park: 8 last week vs. 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.92, 220% spike)
Three related metrics spiking simultaneously suggests systemic park maintenance failure
reporting_angles: Visit major UES parks (Central Park borders, Madison Square Park vicinity) to document litter/maintenance conditions and photograph broken baskets
Interview Parks Department on staffing levels and maintenance schedules; ask whether rodent or wildlife complaints triggered park rules enforcement increase

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting and Urban Disorder
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints jumped 540% to 4 complaints 2 weeks ago versus 0.6 weekly average, coupled with a 227% spike in panhandling complaints (9 vs. 2.8 over same period)—signaling emerging public disorder in high-visibility areas of the Upper East Side.
evidence: Illegal posting: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 3.94, 540% spike)
Panhandling complaints: 9 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average (z-score: 3.81, 227% spike)
Both issues concentrate in same 2-week window, suggesting linked public space occupation
reporting_angles: Map where illegal postings and panhandling complaints cluster—likely along commercial corridors like Madison or Lexington Ave
Interview local business owners and Community Board members about enforcement gaps; ask whether posting relates to specific event, construction, or vendor activity

themes_detail.label: Long-Term Heat/Hot Water Crisis (Baseline High)
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints remain chronically elevated at 1,444 over 90 days—the second-highest complaint category in CD 108—indicating a structural problem in aging residential buildings, though this week's specific spike rate is unknown.
evidence: 1,444 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (second-highest 311 category, after illegal parking at 1,617)
Ongoing problem suggests systemic building maintenance or boiler failure patterns rather than acute crisis
Correlates with CB 108's repeated budget request for 'renovate interior building component' (Department of Education and housing facilities)
reporting_angles: Analysis: Which buildings/blocks generate repeat complaints? Are they rent-stabilized, NYCHA, or private market? Interview HPD about violation enforcement
Winter story: Profile a family dealing with no heat; cross-reference 311 data with housing court filings for habitability disputes
